system.description: Lackeys and hordes: the rank and file foes that support more dangerous combatants. A minion's value is that of half an enemy NPC, or one-third for a Swarm minion.
Silent deathdealers and light-footed bounty hunters: strikers that prey on isolated foes with damage and bleeding effects.
Battlefield physicians and healing magi: supporters that keep allies in the fight with healing and barrier.
Raging beasts and the men that fight like them: armored strikers that break down enemy formations and bite down on defenses.
Bastions and plated shieldbearers: impenetrable defenders that protect allies and areas alike and respond to aggression with heavy attacks.
Spearmen and bodyguards: reactionary defenders with unparalleled control over the battlefield.
Headsmen, intimidators, and knaves: inevitable controllers that crush enemies in a single attack.

_abilityIds.name: Executioner: In the Name of God

system.description: Fiends, demons, and dragons: disruptive strikers with high health pools, customizable into adaptive terrors.
A spider's web, gladiator's net, or a burning field: special controllers that create harmful areas of difficult terrain and nest within them.
Witch hunters, arcane terrors, or disablers of technology: despair-inducing controllers that destroy enemy Focus Pools before finishing them off.
A defensive grid or a healing aura: special supports that project an area of aid that they alone control.
War mages, mortar teams, and artillerizing emplacements: an artillery unit that locks down an area with a constant barrage that can hit multiple foes.
Marksmen and snipers: deadly strikers that can control a battlefield from afar with a choice of weapon.
Eldritch esoterics, adepts of motion, and spatial anomalies. Positional controllers with high health pools, capable of teleporting allies or taking a foe hostage.
Infantry and shocktroopers: versatile strikers that work together to break an opposing line.
Oathkeepers and sword-saints: defensive strikers that use special abilities after marking individual enemies for death.
